newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $20 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $20 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $20 a tonne lower on Wednesday, as traders expected a technical correction after Tuesday's rally to nine-year highs.

New York cocoa futures ended broadly higher on Tuesday, on chart-driven speculative buying amid continued concerns that El Nino could bring dry weather to cocoa growing regions. September cocoa rose $16 a tonne, to $1,712, after ranging between a new life-of-contract high of $1,737 and $1,685.

Spot July finished up $8, to $1,680, after rising to a fresh contract high of $1,700, the highest nearby level on the continuous weekly charts since May 1988. The back months -- which also set lifetime highs -- climbed $17 to $25.
"The specs and funds are all loaded up long and we may shake some guys out," said one trader. "It is still too early for all this talk of smaller crops and El Nino."
Technically, strong support in the September contract was pegged near $1,654, traders said.

In London, cocoa futures erased early gains and eased at midsession on Wednesday, on light profit-taking on the heels of Tuesday's run-up to one-year highs. LIFFE September was down four stg at the break, to 1,142 stg, after peaking at 1,150 stg.
